given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans are lent on 03-02 with `dueOn` 03-16, and today is set to 03-17.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs on a fresh database, so no reminders exist yet.

then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must contain exactly the two reminders, so skipping the call would fail.
Each sent entry must carry the right `memberId`, `loanId` and `dueOn`.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The reminders table must hold exactly the two rows with `sent_on` 2026-03-17.
B3's test proves a refused loan is not recorded, and `mutants.json` names it as covered there.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The first run records a reminder for loan1, and the second run is the one that must skip it.
loan2 is overdue and then returned through the API before the job runs.
loan3 is lent on 03-03, so its `dueOn` is 03-17, which equals today and tests the boundary.

then.why: `toMatchObject` on an array also checks its length, so `sent` must be exactly [loan1]. A resend, a returned loan or a not-yet-due loan would each fail it.

given.why: `refuseFor(loan1, ...)` makes the fake return a refusal for loan1.
The service test only uses a refusal. B5's test shows an unreachable API is turned into the same refused result.
The job runs with an overdue loan whose send is refused.

then.why: The reminders table must hold only loan2's row.
`toContainEqual` matches the exact level and event.
The fields must equal `{ loanId: loan1, error: "Notifications API answered 503" }`.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 has the earlier due date and is refused, yet loan2 is still sent. If the job stopped at the first failure, loan2 would not be sent.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs to completion.

then.why: The last log entry must have level `info` and event `reminders.finished`.
The fields must equal `{ sent: 2, failed: 1 }`. The two counts differ, so they can't be swapped or dropped unnoticed.

given.why: A concrete reminder is passed straight to the real client.

then.why: The recorded request must have method POST and pathname `/notifications`, and the client is built on `NOTIFY_URL`.

then.part: with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The content type must be `application/json` and the body must equal the exact object.
202, 200 and 204 are each accepted, so a check for 200 only would fail.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives kind `refused` and a reason containing "400".

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error gives kind `refused` and a reason containing "unreachable".
